items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: My father is a jazz trumpeter and he was in the Ray Charles band back in the early sixties, with Hank Crawford and Marcus Belgrade and all those guys

ctx.x: And was there a point, a definite point in your life that you said music, that’s it for me; that’s going to be my career.

Yeah. As a matter of fact it’s funny, I just answered that question earlier today in Doc’s history class. And it was around the time when I was about maybe a junior in high school that I said I think music is the direction I’m going to go. Both my parents are musicians and educators as well. My father is a jazz trumpeter and he was in the Ray Charles band back in the early sixties, with Hank Crawford and Marcus Belgrade and all those guys, and “Fathead” Newman. And my mother is a classical pianist and organist…

What do you think, well some people talk about a significant big break or somebody took extra time with you and that caused a good shift for you. Was there a moment like that for you? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
